_comment: Field geometry measured from a real Egyptian National ID card, replacing the synthetic-derived
defaults in layout.py. Coordinates only — the card's print layout is the same on every card,
so nothing here is personal to the card it was measured from.
Two structural corrections over the defaults:
1. The card is RTL. Every field is right-aligned toward x=0.95, and the back's
gender / religion / marital-status row runs right-to-left. The default maritalStatus box
sat at x 0.06-0.36, which on a real card is blank laminate.
2. Front text sits lower than the defaults assumed: the name box was catching the
'بطاقة تحقيق الشخصية' header, and the address box's top edge was reaching into the
second name line, which is why the address came back with name fragments spliced in.
The expiry box previously extended to y=0.66, overlapping the 2D barcode that occupies the
bottom half of the back. Recognition over a barcode returns confident nonsense.
